newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end down, golds spur late rally.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end down, golds spur late rally.

text.p: South African stocks took a tumble on Wednesday as a morning slump in the industrials sector, spurred by futures trade, dragged the all-share index down.
In a reversal of Tuesday's trade the index was caught between a tumbling industrials sector and a resurgent gold index, seeking to claw back some of its recent falls.
"The industrials came under a lot pressure from futures in the morning and that dragged things down," one dealer said.
The overall index ended at 6,780.0, down 9.2 points, with industrials sliding 34.0 points to 7,991.9.
But the market bounced off its day lows in a late afternoon rally as the gold index tracked upwards when fears over a falling bullion price started to fade. Gold in London fixed higher at $383.50.
A wage deal between South Africa's Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers also provided some positive sentiment as it averted the prospect of a damaging strike.

The gold index ended up 26 points at 1,747.2 and gold futures also edged up at 1,208/13 from 1,204. But dealers pointed out the gains in golds had only won back half the losses seen on Monday and Tuesday.
